# Inflation Explainer AI

> Inflation Explainer AI is a free web app built by students of the ByteBusters Coding Club, Yewa College, Ilaro (Odu'a Investment Foundation), Nigeria. A user types an item with its old and new price; the website's code calculates the exact change, the monthly change and what ₦1,000 is worth now, and an AI explains the likely causes and coping tips in simple English or one of 16 other Nigerian languages.

Key facts:
- The maths is always done by code, never by the AI. The AI may only use the numbers given to it.
- National and state figures come from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) CPI report, updated monthly around the 15th. The page never makes up prices.
- Family Basket: a household enters its own monthly items and prices to get its own inflation rate and the items that pushed it up most.
- Price Watch board: year-on-year food and headline inflation by state, with "awaiting NBS update" where no figure exists.
- Learning tool, not financial advice.

## Page
- [Inflation Explainer AI](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/): price check, Family Basket, Price Watch, how it works, FAQ

## Why prices rise (one page per item; reasons, not prices)
- [Why is the price of rice going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/rice/): Rice costs more mainly because of transport and farming costs for local rice, the exchange rate and import rules for foreign rice, and losses from floods and insecurity in rice-growing areas.
- [Why is the price of garri going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/garri/): Garri costs more when cassava is scarce or dearer, when processing costs rise, and when transport from producing villages gets more expensive.
- [Why is the price of beans going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/beans/): Beans cost more because most are grown in the north and carried long distances, harvests are hit by pests, weather and insecurity, and storage losses are high.
- [Why is the price of bread going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/bread/): Bread costs more because wheat flour is imported, and bakeries also pay more for sugar, butter, diesel and packaging.
- [Why is the price of tomatoes going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/tomatoes/): Tomatoes swing in price more than almost any food: they are cheap in the main harvest season and expensive in the off season, and many spoil on the long road to market.
- [Why is the price of pepper going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/pepper/): Pepper prices rise in the off season and when transport from growing areas costs more, because it spoils quickly.
- [Why is the price of onions going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/onions/): Onions cost more when the northern harvest is poor or delayed, when storage losses are high, and when the long journey south costs more.
- [Why is the price of yam going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/yam/): Yam is dearest before the new yam harvest, when old stocks are low, and cheaper after it. Transport and labour costs add to this.
- [Why is the price of plantain going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/plantain/): Plantain costs more in its low season and when transport from the southern growing areas rises.
- [Why is the price of maize (corn) going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/maize/): Maize costs more when harvests are poor, and because people, poultry farms and feed mills all compete to buy the same grain.
- [Why is the price of palm oil going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/palm-oil/): Palm oil costs more in the low production season, when processing and transport cost more, and when the world price is high.
- [Why is the price of vegetable (groundnut) oil going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/vegetable-oil/): Vegetable oil costs more because of world oil-seed prices, the exchange rate, and factory and packaging costs.
- [Why is the price of eggs going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/eggs/): Eggs cost more mainly because chicken feed costs more. Feed is mostly maize and soybean, and it is the biggest cost of a poultry farm.
- [Why is the price of chicken going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/chicken/): Chicken costs more because feed, day-old chicks, medicine and power cost more, and demand jumps at festive times.
- [Why is the price of beef (meat) going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/beef/): Beef costs more because cattle travel long distances from the north, insecurity disrupts herding, and feed and transport cost more.
- [Why is the price of fish going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/fish/): Fish costs more because much frozen fish is imported, fish feed is dear for local farms, and cold storage needs constant power.
- [Why is the price of sugar going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/sugar/): Sugar costs more because Nigeria imports most of its raw sugar, so the exchange rate and world price drive it.
- [Why is the price of milk going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/milk/): Milk costs more because most milk powder is imported, and packaging and factory power cost more.
- [Why is the price of instant noodles going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/noodles/): Noodles cost more because they are made from imported wheat flour and palm oil, in factories that pay more for power and packaging.
- [Why is the price of wheat flour going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/flour/): Flour costs more because wheat is imported and paid for in dollars, and mills run on expensive power.
- [Why is the price of groundnuts going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/groundnuts/): Groundnut prices rise before the new harvest and when insecurity or poor rain cuts the northern crop.
- [Why is the price of sachet (pure) water going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/sachet-water/): Sachet water costs more because the nylon, the treatment chemicals, generator fuel and delivery all cost more.
- [Why is the price of petrol going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/petrol/): Petrol costs more when crude oil prices rise, when the naira is weaker, and when government changes how fuel is priced or subsidised.
- [Why is the price of diesel going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/diesel/): Diesel costs more for the same reasons as petrol: world oil prices and the exchange rate. Because lorries and generators use it, it pushes up many other prices.
- [Why is the price of cooking gas going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/cooking-gas/): Cooking gas costs more when the world price of gas rises, the naira weakens, or supply to depots is tight.
- [Why is the price of kerosene going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/kerosene/): Kerosene costs more because of world oil prices, the exchange rate and limited local supply.
- [Why is the price of charcoal and firewood going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/charcoal/): Charcoal and firewood cost more when gas and kerosene get dearer and more families switch to them, and as trees near towns run out.
- [Why is the price of transport fares (bus, keke, okada) going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/transport-fare/): Fares rise when petrol, spare parts, tyres and engine oil cost more, because drivers must cover those costs from each trip.
- [Why is the price of electricity (light bill) going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/electricity/): Electricity bills rise when tariffs are increased so that they cover the real cost of gas, the exchange rate and running the power network.
- [Why is the price of data bundles and airtime going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/data/): Data costs more when networks pay more for diesel at their masts, imported equipment and taxes, and the regulator approves a tariff rise.
- [Why is the price of school fees going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/school-fees/): School fees rise because schools pay more for salaries, books, power, buses and maintenance, just as families pay more for food and transport.
- [Why is the price of house rent going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/rent/): Rent rises when building materials cost more, more people move into a town than there are houses, and landlords raise rent to keep up with their own costs.
- [Why is the price of cement going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/cement/): Cement costs more because making it uses a great deal of energy, and because of transport, machine parts priced in dollars and strong demand.
- [Why is the price of medicines going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/medicine/): Medicines cost more because most are imported or made from imported ingredients, so the exchange rate drives the price.
- [Why is the price of soap and detergent going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/soap-and-detergent/): Soap and detergent cost more because of palm oil and chemical prices, packaging, factory power and transport.
- [Why is the price of sanitary pads going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/sanitary-pads/): Sanitary pads cost more because the materials are imported and factory, packaging and transport costs have risen.
- [Why is the price of clothes and shoes going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/clothes/): Clothes cost more because fabric and many finished clothes are imported, and tailors pay more for power, thread and rent.
- [Why is the price of phones and laptops going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/phones/): Phones and laptops cost more because they are imported and priced in dollars, with duties and shipping on top.
- [Why is the price of books and stationery going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/books-and-stationery/): Books cost more because paper and ink are imported and printing uses a lot of power.
- [Why is the price of fertiliser going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/fertiliser/): Fertiliser costs more because its ingredients follow world gas and mineral prices and the exchange rate, with transport on top.
- [Why is the price of animal and poultry feed going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/animal-feed/): Feed costs more when maize and soybean are scarce or dear, since they are its main ingredients.
- [Why is the price of cassava going up in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/prices/cassava/): Cassava costs more when demand from garri, flour and starch makers is high, and when labour and transport cost more.

## Money words
- [What is inflation?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/what-is-inflation/): Inflation is when the prices of most things rise over time, so the same money buys less than before.
- [What causes inflation in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/what-causes-inflation/): Inflation in Nigeria is mostly caused by higher costs of fuel, transport and imports, a weaker naira, food supply problems, and more money chasing the same goods.
- [What is the Consumer Price Index (CPI)?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/what-is-cpi/): The Consumer Price Index is a number that tracks the cost of a fixed "basket" of things a typical household buys. Inflation is how fast that number rises.
- [What is food inflation?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/what-is-food-inflation/): Food inflation is how fast food prices alone are rising. It matters most to families who spend a large share of their money on food.
- [What is the exchange rate and why does it change prices?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/what-is-the-exchange-rate/): The exchange rate is how many naira you need to buy one unit of another currency, such as the dollar. When the naira is weaker, everything imported costs more naira.
- [What is a subsidy?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/what-is-a-subsidy/): A subsidy is money the government pays so that people can buy something for less than it really costs.
- [What do supply and demand mean?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/supply-and-demand/): Supply is how much of something is available to buy. Demand is how much people want to buy. When demand is higher than supply, the price rises.
- [What is purchasing power?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/purchasing-power/): Purchasing power is what your money can actually buy. Inflation reduces it.
- [What is shrinkflation?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/what-is-shrinkflation/): Shrinkflation is when the price stays the same but the product gets smaller: a lighter loaf, a thinner bar of soap, fewer biscuits in the pack.
- [How does the Central Bank fight inflation?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/interest-rates-and-inflation/): The Central Bank raises its main interest rate to make borrowing dearer, so people and businesses spend less and prices rise more slowly.
- [Why does my salary feel smaller every year?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/minimum-wage-and-inflation/): Because prices rise every year while most salaries rise only now and then. The gap is a fall in real income.
- [How can a family budget when prices keep rising?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/how-to-budget-in-inflation/): List what you spend, put needs before wants, buy in season and in bulk, and review the list every month because prices change.
- [Does inflation eat my savings?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/saving-and-inflation/): Yes. Money kept in a box or in an account that pays less interest than inflation buys less each year.
- [Why do prices go up fast but come down slowly?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/why-prices-rarely-fall/): Sellers raise prices quickly when their costs rise, but lower them slowly because they are still selling stock bought at the old cost and are unsure the lower cost will last.
- [Who measures inflation in Nigeria?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/who-measures-inflation/): The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) measures inflation. It collects thousands of prices across all states each month and publishes the Consumer Price Index.
- [How does inflation affect students?](https://inflation-explainer.vercel.app/learn/inflation-and-students/): Inflation raises the cost of food, transport, books, data and fees, so the same allowance covers fewer days.
